capabilities: Look up a provision by reference and get literal text with a ready citation
Search statute wording to locate relevant articles
Verify all statutory citations in a note by code, flagging revoked or mismatched text
Expose four lookup and verification tools through a local MCP server
Save chosen statutes into the vault as notes with literal text and hash
disambiguation: Not a legal research or summarization tool; it returns only literal statutory text from its embedded base and does not use a language model.
extras: Desktop only (uses Node.js). main.js is about 11 MB because the legislation base is embedded as readable text; it is only parsed on first use. The base is a snapshot (version 2026.11.17) and does not reflect later legislative changes; state, municipal and less common federal laws are not included. The MCP server listens only on 127.0.0.1 with a token, default port 27190, and Obsidian must stay open. No network access, no telemetry. Interface is in Brazilian Portuguese; MIT license.
intentEvidence: É o irmão do Projurista MCP, que faz o mesmo com súmulas e precedentes qualificados.
motivation: The author's stated idea is that the wording of an article is not written from memory but copied from a checked base.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to retrieve or check exact statutory wording, so legal citations in notes must be written from memory and cannot be verified against a source.

summary: Plugin that embeds 60 Brazilian federal statutes as literal text to look up, cite and verify legal provisions in notes and via a local MCP server.
